notes: Money is converted at release-year World Bank rates and inflated with CPI to 2025 USD.
Films before 1913 have no 2025 USD value (the CPI series starts in 1913), and neither do non-USD amounts from a year without a World Bank rate.
Budgets under $1,000 and revenues under $10,000 are dropped as unreliable.
Money comes from The Numbers, else TMDB, else Wikidata, else the Wikipedia infobox (budget_src, revenue_src); a few amounts checked by hand as wrong are skipped.
Fuzzy title matches to The Numbers are flagged (money_fuzzy, numbers_fuzzy).
Genre shares use 1/n weights: a film with n genres counts 1/n in each.
The TMDB average is null under 50 votes.
Rotten Tomatoes scores of films from 2023 on come from the RT pages (October 2026), older ones from the April 2023 Clapper dump; newer audience scores are often RT's verified score.
Netflix shares cover only matched titles; see the coverage column.
Scores are on 0–100: IMDb, TMDB and Metacritic users ×10, Letterboxd ×20. The Metacritic user score is null under 10 user ratings.
Opening weekend (US only) and estimated home-video sales are inflated with CPI to 2025 USD; both come from The Numbers.
Home-video sales are The Numbers' estimates.
Story source comes from The Numbers, else from the first TMDB keyword that names one (story_source_src); a film with neither has none.
Studio is the group of the first production company that is one of eight major groups, else independent.
Oscar nominations and wins are counted from Wikidata (distinct categories).
Cinema genre shares come from LUMIERE admissions of notable films only; UK and Ireland admissions are LUMIERE estimates, and the combined UK+Ireland market counts as the UK.
attribution: This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
IMDb ratings and votes come from IMDb data via the TMDB+IMDb Kaggle dataset; non-commercial use.

Wikidata (CC0), Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), World Bank (CC BY 4.0), Natural Earth (public domain), FRED / BLS (public domain), Netflix Top 10, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, Letterboxd, The Numbers, LUMIERE (European Audiovisual Observatory).

sources.netflix: Netflix Top 10 chart scores for 94 countries, 2021 to 2026, counted only for titles matched to a film; it says nothing about what people watch outside Netflix.
sources.cinema: Cinema admissions for 36 European markets from LUMIERE (1996 to 2025, notable films only) and The Numbers domestic gross for the US (1980 to 2024); it leaves out every other market, and a market-year needs at least 20 films to be shown.
sources.production: Genre weight of each film made in a country, 1900 to 2026, for films with at least 1,000 IMDb votes; it shows what a country makes, not what its audience watches, and a co-production counts in each of its countries.
